High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad

sentences.text:
?Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:109658
Court No. - 84
Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 5021 of 2023
Applicant :- Azam Khan And 2 Others

Opposite Party :- State Of U.P.And 2 Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Abdul Majeed,Sufia Saba

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Nalin Kumar Srivastava,J.
1.

This application has been moved on behalf of the applicants Azam Khan, Mohd. Azad Khan and Javed Khan seeking anticipatory bail in Case Crime No. 012 of 2023, under Section 376-D IPC,
Police Station Gida, District Gorakhpur.

2. Heard learned counsel for the applicants, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
3.

At the outset, learned counsel for the applicants states that she does not want to press the anticipatory bail application on behalf of applicant no.1 Azam Khan, as he has been arrested by the police.

4. It has been argued by the learned counsel for the applicants that applicants are innocent and they have apprehension of their arrest in the above-mentioned case, whereas there is no credible evidence against them.
Allegations levelled against the applicants are false.

Applicant no.3 is not the resident of Gorakhpur and there was no probability of his presence at the place of occurrence, as Azam Khan And 2 Others vs State Of U.P.And 2 Others on 18 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/1786692/
1 alleged in the F.I.R.

entities.text: Azam Khan And 2 Others vs State Of U.P.And 2 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further submitted that some matrimonial cases are pending between the prosecutrix and her husband wherein her in-laws and Azam Khan, husband of the prosecutrix, have also been falsely implicated.

No internal medical examination report of the prosecutrix is on record,
as she denied for the same.
It is also submitted that applicants have no criminal history.
The investigation of the case is going on.
It has been submitted that in case applicants are granted anticipatory bail, they shall not misuse the liberty of bail and would obey all conditions of bail.

5. Learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail and submitted that in her statements under Sections 161 and 164 CrPC the prosecutrix of the case has corroborated the prosecution version and specific role to both the applicants has been assigned in the alleged crime.
It further submitted that it is a case of gang rape and there is no probability of any false implication of the accused applicant nos. 2 and 3.

Since F.I.R. was not lodged by the police, the prosecutrix was compelled to move application under Section 156(3) CrPC in the Court for registration of F.I.R. and that was the explanation of delay in lodging the F.I.R.

It is further submitted that the applicant nos.
2 and 3 are not cooperating in the investigation and non-bailable warrants have been issued against them.
6. I have considered the rival submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties.

7. It is alleged in present matter that the prosecutrix has some matrimonial dispute with her husband Azam Khan and on 30.7.2022 when she was coming back to her house after pairvi of the case from Civil Court, accused persons, Azam Khan - husband, Mohd. Azad Khan - dever and Javed Khan -nandoi came to her at 7.30 p.m. and dragged her behind the bushes where rape was committed against her by the applicants Azad Khan and Javed Khan.

F.I.R. was not lodged at the police station despite efforts made by her then an application under Section 156(3) CrPC was moved before the Court concerned and by the order of the Court on the siad application, F.I.R. was lodged and investigation is going on.

8. In Sushila Aggarwal and others vs. State (NCT of Delhi) and another, (2020) 5 SCC 1, the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that while considering an application for grant of anticipatory bail, the court has to consider the nature of the offence, the role of the person, the likelihood of his influencing the course of investigation, or tampering with evidence including intimidating witnesses, likelihood of fleeing justice, such as leaving the country, etc.

entities.text: Sushila Aggarwal and others vs. State (NCT of Delhi) and another, (2020) 5 SCC 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It has further been held that Courts ought to be generally guided by considerations such as the nature and gravity of the offences, the role attributed to the applicant, and the facts of the case, while considering whether to grant anticipatory bail, or refuse it.
Whether to grant or not is a matter of discretion.

9. Hence, considering the settled principles of law regarding anticipatory bail, submissions of the learned counsel for the parties, nature of accusation, role of applicants, all attending facts and circumstances of the case, the fact that allegations are serious in nature and the statements of the prosecutrix under Sections 161 and 164 CrPC, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, in my view, it is not a fit case for anticipatory bail to the applicants.
Prayer made in the application is refused.
